issues.claim: Whole audit body (heading through the 'Suggested first step' paragraph and footer line)
issues.problem: Length is roughly 620 words (about 600 excluding title and the 'Prepared from publicly available information' line), well over the ~450-word cap. The three 'Happening now / The agent would / Impact / Pilot' blocks are the bulk of it.
issues.fix: Cut to ~450 words: drop the 'Why this works' bullets to one line, compress each 'Happening now' to one sentence, and trim the opening paragraph to two lines.

issues.claim: Section 1: 'each one keyed by hand' (quote, custom manufacture, certificates of conformance, MTRs, blanket release, stock-and-lock)
issues.problem: Unsupported assertion about internal process. The company's FAQ states a customer can add the COC or MTR SKU to the cart before checkout or contact Customer Service, so certificate requests are at least partly self-service; nothing public says quote or document work is hand-keyed. Presented as fact.
issues.fix: Rewrite as an inference, e.g. 'each of these appears to be prepared by your sales team rather than self-service' or 'these run through your sales team'.

issues.claim: Section 1 impact: 'same-day instead of next-day quote turnaround'
issues.problem: Asserts the company's current quote turnaround is next-day. No public source states a quote turnaround time; nothing was found on the quote page, About page or FAQs.
issues.fix: Change to 'faster quote turnaround (to be measured in the pilot)' and drop 'next-day' unless confirmed in discovery.

issues.claim: Section 3: 'you are mid-expansion with new racking and bagging equipment'
issues.problem: Present-tense claim is not supported by the cited videos. The racking video is titled 'Racking Time Lapse | New Warehouse, Better Albany County Fasteners' and was published 2021-03-12; the poly-bagging video 'Poly Bagging Machines at Albany County Fasteners' was published 2017-09-13. Both predate the audit by several years.
issues.fix: Reword to 'you moved into the 25,000 sq ft warehouse with new racking (2021) and run poly-bagging equipment' or drop the expansion clause.

issues.claim: Section 1: 'Purchasing, fulfillment, marketing and QC each sit with one person'
issues.problem: Purchasing (Peter), fulfillment (Francesca) and marketing (Victoria) are confirmed on the cited blog page, but QC is not a named single-person role there; the blog says Bob personally checks orders for quality. The four-way 'one person each' claim, sourced to that page, is not traceable as stated.
issues.fix: Drop 'QC' or write 'purchasing, fulfillment and marketing each sit with one person, and Bob still checks orders for quality himself'.

issues.problem: Top of range exceeds what the stated assumptions produce. From analysis.json: 1.5 FTE at NJ CSR median $47,740 loaded ~25% = ~$89,500; 50–60% automatable = ~$44,800–$53,700; applying the NBER 14–34% effect gives ~$6,300–$18,300. The stated $25,000 upper bound is about 36% above that ceiling, so the range is inflated rather than conservative.
issues.fix: Restate as '$6,000–$18,000/yr' or explicitly widen the automatable share/effect assumption before quoting a higher band.

issues.claim: Section 2: ratings 'diverge widely by platform ... which suggests older complaints were never answered'
issues.problem: The ratings split is confirmed (4.6/429 on Birdeye, 2.5/21 on Yelp via Yahoo Local), but 'complaints were never answered' imputes a behaviour to the company with no source. The hedge 'suggests' softens it, yet it reads as a factual cause.
issues.fix: Make it explicitly an inference, e.g. 'the older Yelp sample may reflect complaints that went unresolved'.

issues.claim: Sources list: 'Contact page — Mon–Fri 8:00–5:00 EST hours'
issues.problem: Minor citation mismatch. The Contact page shows '8:00am - 5:00pm EST' with no days; the Monday–Friday qualifier appears on the About Us page.
issues.fix: Cite the About Us page for the Monday–Friday wording, or cite both pages.
